reference.title: Kneeling plank (male)
reference.listing: GymVisual page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching knowledge

breathing.pattern: Breathe steadily through the hold with the brace on; do not hold the breath.
breathing.cadence: About one breath every 3 s during the 9 s hold

prescription.progression: Longer holds, then the full front plank on the toes

cues.text: Forearms flat on the mat, elbows under the shoulders, knees down hip width, hips sitting back a little, toes tucked.
Brace the stomach, squeeze the glutes and roll the hips forward until shoulders, hips and knees make one line.
Push the floor away with the forearms, keep the hips level and breathe steadily.
Sit the hips back under control.

mistakes.mistake: Hips left high and behind the knees (piked)
mistakes.fix: Roll the hips forward until shoulder, hip and knee line up.
Brace and squeeze the glutes; tilt the pelvis slightly under.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows far in front of the shoulders
mistakes.fix: Stack the elbows under the shoulders.
Look at the mat just ahead of the hands; neck long.

kinematics.norm: Straight line from shoulders through hips to knees (clinical opinion)
Elbows directly below the shoulders, as in the forearm plank (Schoenfeld 2014 set-up)
From sitting back to neutral (clinical opinion)
Knees on the mat; the knee-supported plank roughly halves abdominal activity compared with the full plank (Escamilla 2016)
Steeper than the full plank because the knees are the base (clinical opinion)
Short holds of 10-30 s for beginners (clinical opinion)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Low back pain that increases in the plank: shorten the hold or drop to the knee plank.
High blood pressure: breathe steadily; long breath-held efforts raise blood pressure.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: hands together (forearms in a slight V) or an incline plank with the forearms on a bench.
Elbow discomfort: fold the mat under the forearms.
regressions: Incline plank with the forearms on a bench.
progressions: Kneeling plank with one arm reaching forward.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and the deep abdominals resist the hips sagging; the knee base shortens the lever so the load is about half the full plank (Escamilla 2016).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: External obliques share the anti-extension work with the rectus abdominis (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: External obliques share the anti-extension work with the rectus abdominis (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Glutes hold the hips forward in line with the knees (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Glutes hold the hips forward in line with the knees (clinical opinion).

phases.label: Forearms and knees down, hips back
Roll the hips into one line

guides.label: Hips roll forward into one line
